topIssues.title: Updating Foundry past 1.8.3 breaks op-deployer tests (no compile cache under deny=warnings; out-of-gas on Amsterdam Sepolia forks)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
We pin Foundry 1.8.3 ([`mise.toml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/mise.toml#L63), [op-deployer `version.json`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/forge/version.json#L2)). That release bundles `webpki-roots` 1.0.9, which still trusts the intermediate CAs from the [eMudhra key compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/). So forge, cast and anvil would accept a forged certificate on their RPC, explorer and solc downloads. 1.8.6 fixes this, but bumping to it fails `go-tests` on #23608, so that PR now only bumps cargo-release and nextest. Both failures start with Foundry **1.8.4**; I bisected 1.8.3 → 1.8.6 locally.

## 1. No compile cache under `deny = "warnings"`

foundry-rs/foundry#17202 (in 1.8.4, fixing foundry-rs/foundry#17174) turns caching off whenever the deny level includes warnings: `set_cached(cached && !self.deny.warnings())`. Cached artifacts don't keep compiler diagnostics, so a warm cache could slip past `--deny warnings`. contracts-bedrock sets [`deny = "warnings"`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/packages/contracts-bedrock/foundry.toml#L80), so from 1.8.4 on:

- `forge build` never writes `cache/`, and every `forge build`/`test`/`script` in contracts-bedrock compiles from scratch. That includes the [script-cache pre-warm](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/packages/contracts-bedrock/justfile#L25-L39) and op-deployer's embedded `artifacts.tzst`.
- `TestDeploySuperchain_WithForge_ManualCall` and `TestNewDeploySuperchainScriptForge` fail their no-recompile assertions ([1](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/superchain_test.go#L175), [2](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/superchain_test.go#L55)).
- CI's forge build cache stops saving anything, and op-deployer users pay a full recompile on every forge-backed script run.

Options:
- **a.** Build and run scripts with `--deny never` (or `FOUNDRY_DENY=never`) wherever we need a cache, i.e. the cache-producing build, the pre-warm and op-deployer's forge client. Enforce warnings in a separate uncached check. This keeps the warning gate but changes how CI enforces it.
- **b.** Drop `deny = "warnings"` from `foundry.toml` and gate warnings only in CI (e.g. `forge build --deny warnings` in a lint job).
- **c.** Ask Foundry to keep the cache under `deny = warnings`, for example by storing diagnostics in it so warm builds can still enforce the gate, and stay on 1.8.3 until then.

## 2. Sepolia-fork tests run out of gas under Amsterdam

From 1.8.4 on, anvil runs a Sepolia fork with the live `Amsterdam` hardfork; 1.8.3 used `Bpo2` (checked with `anvil_nodeInfo`). Sepolia really is on Amsterdam: its headers carry `blockAccessListHash`. The first `deploy-superchain` broadcast, the ProxyAdmin creation, then fails on chain with `OutOfGas`. It uses exactly the 10,221,125 gas that `eth_estimateGas` returned; op-deployer [leaves the gas limit to the node's estimate](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/broadcaster/keyed.go#L118). Affected: `TestSuperchain/sepolia`, `TestApplyDefaultsSP1VerifierOnSepolia`, `TestManageAddGameTypeV2_Integration`, `TestInteropMigration`. Against the same RPC with everything else equal, anvil 1.8.3 passes and 1.8.4–1.8.6 fail.

That anvil's own estimate is insufficient for its own execution points at an anvil estimation bug under Amsterdam. I haven't checked whether a real Sepolia node (geth) estimates this deployment correctly. So whether live op-deployer deployments to Sepolia are affected is still open, and should be answered first.

Options:
- **a.** Pin the hardfork in fork tests via the existing [`devnet.WithHardfork`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-service/testutils/devnet/anvil.go#L72) in [`NewForkedSepolia`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5de51bfd7d67ef42122db9015677da4d9c9896ab/op-service/testutils/devnet/canned.go#L42). This is quick, but the tests then stop matching Sepolia.
- **b.** Add gas headroom in op-deployer's broadcaster (estimate × buffer). This also protects live deployments if real nodes underestimate too.
- **c.** Reproduce outside op-deployer and report it to Foundry if anvil's Amsterdam estimate is wrong.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: kona-node: record safe heads into kona-safedb
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473.

## Scope

Write the local-safe head into `kona-safedb` when the engine confirms it, keyed by the L1 block the derivation pipeline was at when the attributes were confirmed. Record the pipeline's origin at confirmation time, not the block's own `l1_origin`: a span batch can place a block's origin well before the L1 block whose data completed its derivation.

Truncate the database:

- on pipeline reset, to the resume point, re-recording the reset head there (`safe_head_reset` semantics);
- at EL-sync completion, to the head derivation resumes from, and resume derivation from the safedb tip when it is older than the EL's safe head (parity with #21111).

Failure policy: a missing entry is served as an older safe head, not as an error, so writes are retried with backoff and the actor stops the node once retries are exhausted. Continuing past a failed write is not an option.

## Starting point

The closed PR #22514 implemented this against the derivation actor and has a fixture where the pipeline origin and the block's `l1_origin` differ. Revive it against today's actors instead of waiting on #22527.

## Done

- [ ] Writes happen at local-safe promotion with the pipeline origin as the key.
- [ ] Both truncation paths are implemented and unit-tested, including a reset that predates all records.
- [ ] Retry and fail policy is implemented and unit-tested.
- [ ] `safedb-reviewer` passes on the diff.

topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:

Failed in the merge queue on #23608, which only bumps the cargo-release and nextest pins in `mise.toml`.

The proposer submitted **2** log batches where the test expects exactly 1 ([`zk_proposer_test.go#L291-L294`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/71fd222d1e7a205b300e4b377f2d95d177f5a0d0/op-acceptance-tests/tests/proofs/zk/zk_proposer_test.go#L291-L294)). The metric already read 2 at 11:54:40, about 1.5 minutes into the run, and stayed at 2 until the wait timed out at 12:04:40. So this is a real second batch, not a slow metric. The check at [`zk_proposer.go#L97`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/71fd222d1e7a205b300e4b377f2d95d177f5a0d0/op-devstack/dsl/zkproposer/zk_proposer.go#L97) then failed after 762s:

topPRs.title: kona-node!: simplify engine RPC clients and servers
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Engine RPC reads previously crossed queue clients and actors that added indirection to ordinary request handling. Kona now uses concrete Alloy-backed engine clients, serves rollup reads directly, and centralizes request observability in JSON-RPC middleware.

HTTP and WebSocket serve the remaining modules. The unused `dev` and `ws` RPC modules and `--rpc.ws-enabled` flag are removed; WebSocket is always available. Downstream Rust users must adopt the concrete `EngineClient`, remove client type parameters, and use `EngineQueryClient::output_at_block` for output reads. Metrics instrumentation is always compiled. The end-to-end tests now exercise ordinary rollup RPC methods over WebSocket instead of the removed subscriptions.

Third PR in the stack: #23220 → #23227 → this PR → #23258 → #23229 → #23223 → #22307. The five task-to-helper commits are isolated in #23258 above this PR.

Each retained intermediate RPC/helper commit compiles. The RPC tip passes 308 focused Rust tests; the final rebased stack passes 323, full Rust and Go lint, both validator and sequencer runtime suites (13 passed and one existing skip each), the restart suite, and conductor runtime coverage. Rust, Go, and deletion reviews have no unresolved findings.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: add spn-wallet to fund and inspect SPN requesters
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
With op-signer, the op-zk-proposer SPN requester is a KMS key that can sign only SPN messages. It cannot deposit PROVE for itself, and operators have no tool to fund it. `spn-wallet` funds any SPN account from another signer, `PRIVATE_KEY` or a GCP Cloud KMS key, and the recipient signs nothing. It also reads balances, history, proof requests and bids without a key. The README's "Funding the SPN requester" section is the runbook.

Write commands preview by default and send only with `--broadcast`. `--max-fee` is then required, and `fund --from-l1` checks it before PROVE leaves L1. `fund` treats the transfer as done once the recipient's history shows the TRANSFER_IN for its hash. A balance check would be wrong here, because a requester pays for proofs while it waits and its balance can stay low after the credit.

Builds on wwared's `feat/spn-wallet` commit, which is kept as the first commit. Refs #21419; the alerting half of that issue is not part of this PR.

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: read replaced optimistic heads through kona-host in the log scan
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body: Follow-up to #23464. When the supernode replaces a block for an invalid interop message, it keeps reporting the denied block as optimistic at its timestamp, but the rewind leaves that block non-canonical, so the L2 node may have pruned it or never had it. The proposer's message scan read every optimistic head from the L2 node by hash, so any game spanning a replaced block failed on every attempt until its deadline. The scan now reads a replaced head through kona-host with the same `L2BlockData` hint the consolidation uses, which re-derives the block from L1 and re-executes it on its canonical parent, so the scan still sees every message the consolidation checks. Span synthesis likewise reads, through kona-host's `L2OutputRoot` hint, the agreed output of a chunk that starts at a replaced timestamp, where the supernode also reports the denied block.

topPRs.title: kona-node!: prefetch sequencer L1 origins and attributes
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Kona no longer waits on L1 origin, header, or receipts RPCs between sealing a block and starting the next build. A supervised single-writer prefetcher prepares linked origins and their attributes inputs together, starts further lookahead on selection, and respects confirmation depth. The max-drift fallback waits at most 500 ms; background RPCs have a separate 10 s deadline so a slower receipts endpoint can still make progress.

An orphaned origin resets the engine instead of eventually stalling at max drift. Canonical rechecks survive cancellations, failed RPCs, partial publication, and head reversals. Prepared parent data remains available when a build fails and retries. Repeated max-drift requests reuse in-flight preparation so slower receipts requests can finish.

Stacked on #23223. Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23281.

BREAKING CHANGE: `L1OriginSelectorError` adds `Pending`, `Timeout`, `Closed`, `NextOriginOrphaned`, and `Attributes` variants. Custom exhaustive matches must handle these preparation and lifecycle outcomes.

Local validation: all 253 tests across the service and its node/lokahi dependents pass with all features and zero skips. The 10s L2 / 12s L1 simulation covers both prefetch/build orderings through the actual worker loop and asserts zero build-path L1 calls. Full workspace lint (formatting, strict Clippy, documentation, and upstream-mirror checks) passes. Rust and adversarial/deletion reviews have no remaining findings. All 79 reported CI checks pass, including `ci-gate`, `required-rust-ci`, `required-rust-e2e`, `required-contracts-ci`, and dependency review. CI also passes Kona sequencer/restart end-to-end tests and memory checks. Full devnet acceptance tests were not run locally.

topPRs.title: kona-node: record the safe head history into kona-safedb
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
kona-node has had the `kona-safedb` crate since #21522 but nothing wrote to it, so a kona-node cannot answer which L1 block made an L2 block safe. op-challenger, op-proposer and op-dispute-mon need that answer, which is why a kona-only verifier set cannot back proofs today.

With this change the derivation actor records every safe head it derives, keyed by the L1 block the attributes were derived from, and truncates the record to the point derivation restarts from on an engine reset and at EL-sync completion. A head the engine adopts without deriving it is never recorded. A write that still fails after retries stops the node: a missing entry is not reported by later queries, it is served as an older safe head, and op-challenger would act on that. For the same reason, when the engine resumes above the recorded tip, the history is cleared rather than left with a gap. A derived block is queued for finalization only once it is recorded, so the engine's finalized head cannot pass the record.

Operators see no change yet. The builder defaults to the disabled database; the CLI flag that opens an on-disk one lands with #23477, and the RPCs that serve the record with #23475 and #23476. The engine now hands derivation the local-safe head instead of the safe head, which is the label the record claims; the two are always equal in kona-node today.

Left for a follow-up on the same issue: making the engine resume derivation from the recorded tip when the tip is older than the head it would otherwise resume from, as op-node does since #21111. That needs the engine actor to read the database and check the tip is canonical. Until it lands, that case clears the history and logs a warning. A metric for it belongs to #23478.

Part of #23474, tracked under #23473. The January design discussion is on Notion: [Derivation Persistence (SafeDB)](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/Derivation-Persistence-SafeDB-2e8f153ee16280548875e0e628b85d94); its record-every-L1-block proposal is #23480.

Reviews run: `safedb-reviewer` and `rust-code-reviewer`. Every finding was applied or is covered by the follow-up above; none was dismissed. Note for reviewers: the actor tests exercise the real rocksdb database, so `kona-node-service`'s test build now needs libclang locally, as `kona-safedb`'s already did.
